question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{(x+y)^{3}}, & x\ge 1,\,y\ge 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

The marginal CDF ${F}_{X}(x)$ of $X$ is given by

$$
{F}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<1 \\ g(x), & x\ge 1.\end{aligned}
$$

What is the function $g(x)?$
question.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, the marginal density function of $X$ for $x\ge 1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{4}{(x+y)^{3}}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={lim}_{b\to \infty }{\int }_{1}^{b}\frac{4}{(x+y)^{3}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =4{lim}_{b\to \infty }{\int }_{1}^{b}(x+y)^{-3}\,\text{d}y \\  & =4{lim}_{b\to \infty }{[-\frac{1}{2}(x+y)^{-2}]}_{y=1}^{y=b} \\  & =-2{lim}_{b\to \infty }{[\frac{1}{(x+y)^{2}}]}_{y=1}^{y=b} \\  & =-2{lim}_{b\to \infty }[\frac{1}{(x+b)^{2}}-\frac{1}{(x+1)^{2}}] \\  & =\frac{2}{(x+1)^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the marginal CDF of $X$ for $x\ge 1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{F}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{x}{f}_{X}(u)\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{x}\frac{2}{(u+1)^{2}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =2{\int }_{1}^{x}\frac{1}{(u+1)^{2}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =2{[-\frac{1}{u+1}]}_{1}^{x} \\  & =2[\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{x+1}] \\  & =1-\frac{2}{x+1} \\  & =\frac{x-1}{x+1},\end{aligned}
$$

So, the full expression for ${F}_{X}(x)$ is

$$
{F}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<1 \\ \frac{x-1}{x+1}, & x\ge 1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $g(x)=\frac{x-1}{x+1}.$
